content:
In batteries#1990, @Jovan Gerbscheid updates the on_goal tactic so that it can accept a sequence of numerals so that the tactic block works on all the numbered goals. This is great, but as I said on that PR I would prefer to have some more generic goal management tools.

In particular, I think we should have multi-goal versions of Lean.Elab.Tactic.focus and Lean.Elab.Tactic.focusAndDone, which take, for example, a predicate MVarID → Bool to select which goals to work on. Then it would be nice to have syntax for selecting (i.e., in the setGoals sense) multiple goals:

  1. by index number (as with on_goal)
  2. by (some substring of the) name (like case but without renaming inaccessible names, and not getting only the first goal matching the name)
  3. by pattern matching at reducible transparency

It would be nice to have some unified interface for this. All these should come in a version which doesn't force you to close all the selected goals, and another which does force you to close them all. Moreover, to better isolate this subcollection of goals and the tactics on which they operate, I think it makes sense to require a colGt in the syntax (i.e., colGt " => " tacticSeq).

Of course, we could simply write such a tactic in Mathlib (or Batteries), and in fact, I have something implemented locally, albeit likely not very well, but since this overlaps with case (and, in the => syntax issue, conv) in core, Jovan suggested that we try to coordinate with the FRO here. I would be interested in getting feedback.

These kinds of multi-goal selection mechanisms would be particularly useful for tactics which generate many side goals, and potentially discharge some or else return them to the user. A tactic doing this should sequester the side goals it generates to ensure maintainability.

The underlying implementations of these functions are going to be pretty simple, so I think the real question is what you would imagine the tactic interface to look like. I think for most people this will not be something they need.

I do think that it would be great if on_goal and case could be extended to have the same features, with the only difference being that case has to close the goal and on_goal can leave it unsolved (plus a linter that suggests replacing on_goal with case when possible). However, this requires a change in core, because case is defined there.
